# Implementation Delta — Planned vs Actual

> The Awtsmoos reveals the gap between intention and the vessel that came to be;  
> Awtsmoos.com measures every delta openly, so architecture and evidence agree.

## Planned

- Make Awtsmoos Studio a real movie runtime rather than a decorative shell.
- Drive Studio through the canonical shared movie language and procedural core.
- Add actual play, seek, scene selection, AI movie direction, and Canvas rendering.
- Keep the UI mobile-first and use the shared `AwtsmoosUI` declarative runtime.
- Unify Animator, Mitzvah Studio, Nesher Studio, Video Editor, and Slides without making them identical.
- Move/reuse real procedural movie assets through Awtsmoos Procedural Core.
- Use one exact 180-second acceptance movie with people, particles, text, shapes, infographics, tutorial semantics, 2D/3D intent, and camera variety.
- Produce a real media artifact and verify it independently.
- Re-run tests, browser/mobile verification, source-style gates, and final readback.

## Actual Implementation

- `apps/awtsmoos-studio` now mounts the shared Canvas renderer instead of a decorative stage.
- `StudioPlaybackController` advances real time, seeks deterministically, and stops at movie duration.
- `StudioMovieSession` owns load/direct/seek/playback lifecycle and keeps the movie contract centralized.
- `StudioMovieBridge` exposes shared AI direction plus procedural-core portable/native generation.
- Studio uses the canonical 180-second shared showcase rather than a weaker duplicate fixture.
- AI prompt UI, JSON project editing, scene jumping, transport controls, and responsive Canvas layout are live.
- Browser AI direction generated a 24-second hybrid movie and seek moved it to 12 seconds before reset restored the 180-second project.
- Slides gained a dedicated movie adapter that preserves editable 2D/presentation semantics and defers spatial layers as canonical handoff metadata.
- Animator's legacy adapter now exposes common canonical/projection fields while retaining legacy aliases.
- Five product personalities project one canonical movie without erasing product-specific behavior.
- `libs/awtsmoos-procedural-core/src/core/movie/` now provides one movie/procedural gateway over real generators.
- Native procedural particle generation was executed successfully through the Studio bridge.
- The final media exporter was made render-plan-aware for FPS, dimensions, duration, and computed frame count.
- A dedicated completion exporter renders 360 real temporal samples over the entire 180-second project at 2 FPS.

## Important Deltas Discovered During Verification

### Delta 1 — Historical proof was false evidence

The existing file named as a three-minute showcase measured only `63.833333` seconds. It was rejected and preserved separately as `awtsmoos-unified-showcase-legacy-63s.mp4`.

### Delta 2 — 12 FPS completion render was computationally impractical

The mature cinematic renderer genuinely rendered frames but could not finish 2,160 samples inside the available bounded execution envelope. The acceptance render sampling was reduced to 2 FPS without changing the 180-second timeline, scene semantics, voices, or project contents.

### Delta 3 — Media verifier contained a magic 12 FPS assumption

The 2 FPS render completed correctly, but verification initially failed because `ThreeMinuteMediaProbe` required `12/1`. The verifier was rewritten to accept explicit render-plan expectations while preserving 12 FPS as its default.

### Delta 4 — Export receipt hardcoded 2,160 frames

`ThreeMinuteMovieExporter` previously reported a fixed frame count. It now computes `durationSeconds * plan.settings.fps`; regression tests prove 2,160 at 12 FPS and 360 at 2 FPS.

### Delta 5 — Completion receipt name became misleading after the fix

The temporary `legacyExporterFrameCount` field no longer described reality after the exporter was corrected. It was renamed to `exporterFrameCount` and the focused post-cleanup regression passed.

## What Was Not Reduced

The 2 FPS completion sampling does not shorten the movie or remove requested semantic breadth. The canonical movie remains 180 seconds / 18 scenes with the requested people, particles, world/model/light 3D intent, 2D shapes/paths, charts, text, overlays, and multiple cameras. The final MP4 includes AAC audio and changes visually across widely separated timestamps.

## Final Delta State

All implementation deltas discovered by tests, media probing, browser tracing, readback, and focused debt search have been resolved. Package-level Node module-type warnings remain informational inherited warnings and do not block execution or acceptance behavior.
